findings.evidence: Round-2 reviewed manifest hash was e308a0d65417d1cec2bccf46f0d26eb88e61a8e6624905a78ad11d6100ad3ab8, but its design/catalog/ledger bindings still point to previous values rather than the reviewed physical-gap and fixture-control corrections; implementation-design-granularity reproduces DESIGN_HASH_DRIFT.
findings.risk: A review artifact could be associated with stale bytes rather than the corrected design, so the mechanical review identity would not be trustworthy.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: Round-1 repairs were independently verified: 45/68 source-evidence partition is honest and U06 owns fixture/OpenAPI closure, but the review object was not bound to these current bytes.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: Rebinding current hashes is smaller and safer than weakening the checker or accepting prose about unbound current bytes.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The correction changes only design evidence binding and does not expand business, API, runtime or dynamic scope.

conclusion.summary: The two Round-1 substantive findings are closed, but the reviewed manifest had stale design/catalogue/ledger hashes. The final review hard-stops after this finding; only post-remediation binding and Claude recheck are permitted.
